newsitem.title: USA: No more FBI agents to be charged over Ruby Ridge.
newsitem.headline: No more FBI agents to be charged over Ruby Ridge.

text.p: After a prolonged investigation the Justice Department announced Friday it would not prosecute any more FBI agents over the 1992 Ruby Ridge shooting and its aftermath.
Justice officials may explore further disciplinary action against other agents, but none will face criminal charges, according to a statement released by the department.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation said in a statement that four FBI employees who had been targets of the criminal probe would remain on paid leave until the administrave review is complete.

One Federal Bureau of Investigation agent, Michael Kahoe, has pleaded guilty to obstructing justice by concealing and destroying an internal review of the deadly 1992 shootout in Ruby Ridge, Idaho. Sentencing is set for next month.

The federal sieges at Ruby Ridge and Waco, Texas a year later, became rallying cries for right-wing militias and were cited by the defense counsel at the trial of Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh as contributory factors leading up to the bombing.
Kahoe was accused of destroying a document related to the murder trial of white separatist Randy Weaver -- the key figure in the Ruby Ridge affair.

A Senate Judiciary subcommittee was very critical of the FBI after its hearings into the matter and Judiciary chairman Sen. Orrin Hatch, a Utah Republican, said he would consult with his colleagues when the Senate reconvenes in September.
Weaver's wife and young son were shot to death by federal agents; Weaver was acquitted in the killing of a U.S. marshal.

Weaver and his friend, Kevin Harris, were charged with the murder of Deputy U.S. Marshal William Degan, who was shot and killed in a confrontation Aug. 21, 1992. Weaver's son was killed in the firefight.

After the shootout, the FBI's hostage rescue team went to Ruby Ridge, and on Aug. 22 an FBI sniper fired two shots at the cabin, wounding Weaver and killing his wife Vicki. The standoff ended nine days later when Weaver surrendered.
A dozen FBI agents have received some kind of disciplinary action in the case. In adition to Kahoe, four have been placed on administrative leave with pay.
The investigation into the agents' role was spearheaded by Michael Stiles, U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. Attorney General Janet Reno approved his recommendations.
